title: Cheers Emoji 🍻 Meaning: Clinking Beer Mugs Explained
description: The 🍻 clinking beer mugs emoji means “cheers.” People use it to toast good news, thank a friend, confirm plans and celebrate together. See how it works.
summary: The 🍻 clinking beer mugs emoji means “cheers.” It is used to toast good news, congratulate someone, agree to plans and celebrate with friends. It also works as a friendly sign-off meaning thanks or “well done,” even when nobody is actually drinking.
meaning: Two mugs knocking together is a gesture, not just a drink, and that is the difference between 🍻 and the single beer. It reproduces the moment of a toast. People send it when a friend gets a job, when a team wins, when the weekend begins, or when plans are confirmed. The message is togetherness: we are raising a glass to this, whether or not there are glasses.

Because of that, it often works as a reply all by itself. Someone shares good news and 🍻 comes back in place of “congratulations.” Someone settles an argument and 🍻 means “no hard feelings.” In British and Australian English, where “cheers” also means “thanks” or “goodbye,” the emoji takes on those senses too, ending messages the way a nod would. It has a comradely, back-slapping quality.

As a plan, it is more social than 🍺. “🍻 tonight?” implies a group, a bar and probably more than one round. It dominates posts about birthdays at pubs, reunions, bachelor parties, post-game celebrations and beer festivals. Between men especially, it is a common way to express warmth without sentimentality. A toast says what a hug might, at a comfortable distance.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It answers good news, seals plans and ends friendly exchanges. “See you at 8 🍻” confirms a night out. “You got the apartment?! 🍻” is congratulations. After a favor, it means thanks and that drinks are owed. A lone 🍻 as a reply is rarely misread; it is agreement and goodwill.

contexts.label: In sports
contexts.body: Fans toast wins with it and console each other after losses. It appears in match-day threads, fantasy league chats and posts from the pub. Rival supporters who have been trading jabs may end with 🍻 to show the banter was in good spirit.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Team wins, launches and farewells bring it out, as do Friday afternoon messages. It is friendly and usually acceptable in casual workplaces. As with any alcohol emoji, some colleagues do not drink, so 🎉 or 🙌 may suit a mixed or formal audience better.

examples.meaning: Celebrating good news and inviting friends to toast.

examples.text: Appreciate you covering for me, mate 🍻
examples.meaning: Thanking a friend, in the British sense of “cheers.”
Confirming plans for a night out.

examples.text: Tough loss but great season. 🍻 lads
examples.meaning: Raising a glass in consolation and solidarity.
Ending a debate on friendly terms.

combos.meaning: A deal made or a disagreement settled amicably.

confusedWith.difference: 🍺 is a single beer: the drink, a craving or a solo pint. 🍻 is the act of toasting with someone. Use the pair when the point is celebration or company.
🥂 shows champagne flutes and suits weddings, anniversaries, New Year's Eve and formal congratulations. 🍻 is the casual, pub-level version of the same gesture.
🤝 signals agreement or a deal without any festivity. 🍻 adds celebration and friendship to the agreement.

avoid: Avoid it for solemn occasions, such as condolences, unless you know a toast to the person's memory would be welcome.
Don't use it with people who avoid alcohol, for whom a different celebratory emoji is more considerate.
Leave it out of formal congratulations to clients or senior colleagues.
design: Two foaming glass beer mugs tilt toward each other and touch at the rim. Most platforms add small motion lines or droplets of foam at the point of contact to show the clink. The mugs match the single beer mug design of each vendor, so the pair looks consistent with it on every device.

faqs.q: What does 🍻 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Typically “cheers”: congratulations, thanks, agreement or an invitation to go for drinks. It is a friendly, buddy-like emoji. If he sends it to someone he is interested in, it suggests a casual night out more than romance.

faqs.q: What does 🍻 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: The same thing. She is toasting something, confirming plans or celebrating with you. It is cheerful and sociable and does not usually carry flirtatious meaning unless the rest of the conversation does.

faqs.q: Can I use 🍻 if I don't drink?
faqs.a: Yes. Many people use it simply to mean “cheers” or “well done,” with no alcohol involved. If you prefer to avoid the association entirely, the clinking glasses or a party popper conveys a similar spirit.

Formality. Beer mugs are for casual wins, friends and pubs. Champagne flutes are for elegant or milestone occasions such as engagements and New Year's Eve. Either one can accompany a simple “congratulations.”

faqs.q: When was the clinking beer mugs emoji added?
faqs.a: It has been in the standard emoji set since 2010, released alongside the single beer mug, which is why the two designs always match on a given platform.
